question: When two real follower ReadIndex requests are batched by confirmation of the newer context, does the leader return each originating request context to its own follower?
rationale: The leader drains older readStatus records on confirmation of the newest context, but handleReadIndexLeaderConfirmation uses m.Hint/m.HintHigh for every forwarded response instead of s.ctx. The probe starts three peers using Launch and real bootstrap entries, persists and applies updates before message publication, elects through Tick, submits two distinct caller contexts through Peer.ReadIndex, loses only the first context heartbeat messages, and otherwise delivers actual messages FIFO. It observes actual ReadyToReads at each originating peer, then delivers three healthy heartbeat intervals. This is a bounded peer-level identity/progress probe; it does not claim an application read, RequestState timeout, or infinite stall. The root caller matches exact contexts in pendingReadIndex.addReady; inspection after actual retained execution must determine the appropriate local obligation. A separate initial suspicion about observer quorum counting is countered by broadcastHeartbeatMessageWithHint excluding observers for nonzero contexts; no observer history is asserted here.
